title: Design System: ReWild — The Field List

graphite.purpose: Pencil ink; all body and heading text and every heavy border. Also the ground of the plant-sheet scrim and of the note bar. The scrim is written as the literal rgba(31,36,32,0.55) in .sheetback rather than as a token — graphite at 55%, used exactly once. Recorded as debt, not canonized: one use is not a system, and the screen palette stays at 14 values.

survey-ink.purpose: Every orange below large size: the unverified line under a rebate figure, the dashed rule above it, and both warn chips — 'outside your band' and 'wants full sun or part shade'.

survey-deep.purpose: The pressed state of the primary action button only. Shares the surveyor ramp; it is the flag under pressure, not a third orange.

stamp-wash.purpose: The translucent white the locality stamp sits on — paper showing through rubber. Only ever over hi-vis; the ramp is alpha, not lightness, because the ground must read through it.

p-page.purpose: The paper the tear-out prints on. Set with !important on body inside @media print together with background-image:none, because the 22px ruling is a screen device and must not be laid down in toner. No screen surface may take it.

p-ink.purpose: All primary print text, section underlines, table-head rules, the pbox checkbox stroke and the dashed warn rules on the sheet.

p-ink-2.purpose: The sheet's meta hand: the serialized header line, section counts, scientific names, program URLs, empty-state notes and the form-number footer.

p-rule.purpose: The light divider on the sheet: 1px solid between table rows, 1px dotted between checklist items.

display.purpose: The landing headline only, capped at 16ch. The only place Archivo 800 gets real size.

headline.purpose: The heading at the top of every in-app view; clamps at 2.1rem.

title.purpose: Section heads, uppercase, underlined by a 2px graphite rule, carrying an optional mono note pushed to the right end of that rule — 'typical requirements · confirm with your program' over the paperwork checklist.

body.purpose: Running copy; ledes cap at 66ch in secondary pencil.

label.purpose: Mono uppercase captions: tabs, buttons, field captions, panel headers, chips, and the month labels down the run.

figure.purpose: Mono tabular running totals: tally band, habitat score, rebate amount.

bundled.weight: 4.68 MB of Wikimedia originals re-encoded to 860 KB total
bundled.record: Each plant record carries `photo` (the relative path) and `credit` ({by, lic, file}).
bundled.credits: CREDITS.md at the root lists all 17 with author, licence and a Commons link.
bundled.attribution: The on-sheet credit line reads `Photo: <by> · <lic> · Wikimedia Commons`, the link built from credit.file. Extraction reads Commons' Artist field, falls back to Attribution, and unwraps the 'No machine-readable author provided' boilerplate, so every attribution-required image resolves to a real name; the four remaining unknowns are Public domain, where none is owed.
bundled.placement: The plant sheet only. Never in a list row — at 58×44 a photograph is mud and the drawn plate reads instantly. Plates and photographs are different jobs, not alternatives.
notes: Bundled, never hotlinked. This build shipped once with 17 dead Wikimedia URLs (files renamed upstream, every one 400ing); hotlinking would re-earn that failure.
A photograph whose licence cannot be verified before download is not shipped at all.
The carries width=560 height=373 so the sheet does not reflow as the file decodes.

user.control: shotSlot(key, label) — one on every planted row and every sighting.
user.storage: Data URIs in S.shots, keyed `p-<symbol>` or `s-<id>`, inside the same localStorage record. Nothing leaves the browser.
user.failure: Over budget, or if save() throws, the app surfaces a plain-language .note-bar and rolls the write back rather than failing silently. Removing a sighting deletes its photograph.
notes: The empty slot is a 1.5px dashed heavy-rule box in mono uppercase — the only dashed border on screen besides the unverified rule, and it reads as a blank waiting to be filled.
Hover fills it hi-vis, consistent with The Hi-Vis Is State Rule: a filled slot is a logged observation.
The stored image renders at max-width 150px inside a 1.5px graphite box — a photo taped to the page beside the entry, not a gallery tile.
The note bar is sheet text on graphite at body size, fixed bottom-centre for 5.2s. It is the system’s only transient surface and carries no icon.

print.medium: The tear-out is its own medium and does not inherit the screen ramp. `.printonly` is display:none on screen and display:block inside @media print, where the app chrome (demo bar, locality band, tally band, index tabs, main, footer) goes display:none !important — and with it .sheetback, .plantsheet and .note-bar, so an open plant sheet or a live note never lands on the printed sheet.

typeScale.name: section note
typeScale.value: mono 8.5pt / 400 in p-ink-2, baseline-aligned at the right end of the head

typeScale.name: table head
typeScale.value: mono 8pt / 700 / +0.08em uppercase over a 1px p-ink underline

typeScale.name: warn line
typeScale.value: mono 8pt in p-ink over a 1px dashed p-ink rule

print.checkbox: `.pbox` — a 10pt square with a 1.2pt p-ink border and no fill. The print counterpart of the 23px screen tick box; both are squares you mark.
sections: Plant list, with a blank QTY column for the nursery counter
Care schedule for the month, as pbox checkboxes
Rebate worksheet, per-program estimate with an unverified warn line
Before you dig, the paperwork checklist
print.serialization: Header reads SHEET 1 OF 1 · REC. BY ____________ · date. Footer reads FORM RW-1 · rewild · every figure unverified · state lives only in the browser it was entered in.
notes: Point sizes, not the rem ramp. Do not 'fix' the print block to screen tokens; the divergence is deliberate and DESIGN.md records it.
The four p-* tokens exist only inside @media print. No screen surface inherits them; the screen palette is unchanged at 14.

Icons take world ink only and never a per-item colour. This is the rule that removed ~15 inherited Material-palette hexes; the wildlife lookup fallback is {label, icon:'ti-circle'} with no colour field.
The CDN URL requires its /dist/ path segment. Without it the stylesheet 404s and every icon silently disappears — the exact bug the superseded build shipped with.
Icons label controls. Species imagery is always the drawn plate set, never an icon.

The measured figure, and the only place it is written: 26 distinct ti-* classes in the shipped source — 12 written directly into markup and 15 supplied by data records for wildlife groups, goals, sun options and marketplace entries, with ti-butterfly in both sets. DESIGN.md deliberately carries no count, because this one went stale three times in three rounds, once per feature that added a glyph. Re-measure here on every sync with grep -o 'ti-[a-z0-9-]*' index.html | sort -u | wc -l.
Panel snippets below inline the same glyphs as SVG at the same stroke weight, because the sidecar renders into a shadow DOM with no webfont loaded.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The only easing curve in the build. Used for every transition.

motion.name: micro-press
motion.purpose: Scale press feedback on buttons, tabs and the tick box (0.97, tick 0.92).

motion.name: micro-state
motion.purpose: Colour changes on rows, chips, options, month cells and the tick fill.

motion.name: sheet-press
motion.purpose: The plant sheet’s close button presses to scale(0.94). The sheet itself has no entrance animation — it is a page you turned to, not a thing that arrived, and animating it would spend the budget The One Moment Rule already commits.

motion.name: rerank-flip
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: FLIP translate on plant rows when a goal changes. Double-guarded by CSS prefers-reduced-motion and a JS matchMedia early return. Light-aware ranking re-sorts through this same moment and added no second one.

motion.name: grid-pitch
motion.purpose: Not motion, but the spatial rhythm every measure answers to.

components.name: Coded Row with Plate
components.description: The unit of the product: mono record code in stamp violet, a drawn growth-form plate, common and scientific name, constraint chips, and a tick box whose check fades in when logged. The plate is now a button (cursor:zoom-in) that opens the plant sheet; on hover its box goes stamp violet on hi-vis. The same .row / .tick pair carries the paperwork checklist, where the code column is dropped and the item text spans to the end at weight 400.

components.name: Photo Slot (Taped-In)
components.description: The user’s own photograph, on every planted row and every sighting. Empty, it is a dashed heavy-rule box in mono uppercase with a camera glyph over a visually hidden file input; filled, it is the image in a 1.5px graphite box at 150px with a surveyor-ink remove control. Images are resized to 640px and re-encoded at q0.7 before storage; the note bar carries the plain-language refusal when the 3.2 MB budget is spent.

Before you dig typical requirements

  • Apply and get written approval BEFORE removing any lawn — nearly every program disqualifies work already done.
  • Photograph the area before you start, from a fixed spot you can shoot again after.

Common requirements across lawn-replacement programs, not any one program’s rules.

narrative.overview:
ReWild is a field book, not an app that happens to be about plants. Every surface behaves like a page of waterproof ruled stock: a cool grey-green ground printed with a real 22px grid, graphite ink, heavy black rules that box the sheet, and a high-visibility cover yellow that marks anything logged, active or tallied. The yard is a running record — dated, coded, tallied rows — and the interface's job is to look like the place that record is kept.

Density is the point. Rows are short, rules are thin and constant, labels are set in mono and shouted small. Nothing floats: there are no shadows anywhere in the build, no rounded corners anywhere in the build, and no soft card surfaces. Depth comes from three tonal grounds (stock behind, sheet in front, shade for pressed and inert regions) separated by 1px printed rules and 2–2.5px graphite borders. Content that reads as a form is drawn as a form: ruled blanks with an underline instead of a box, tick boxes you press, index tabs that sit up over the sheet edge.

This world explicitly refuses the calm-plant-app arrangement — soft cards on a sage ground, generous whitespace, muted pastels, cream paper. The page ground is cool on purpose and is never to be warmed toward cream. Because the image workspace was unavailable, the build is fully code-led: species illustrations are authored SVG plates drawn by growth form, which is what a field guide does anyway.
keyCharacteristics: Printed 22px grid on the page ground, always visible around the sheet
Zero radius, zero shadow, hard graphite rules at 1px / 2px / 2.5px
Hi-vis yellow means state (logged / active / tallied); surveyor orange means action
Azeret Mono is measurement only: codes, figures, tallies, dates, labels
Tonal stack of three grounds — stock, sheet, shade — instead of elevation
Exactly one authored motion moment in the whole build

rules.name: The Two-Orange Rule
rules.body: Surveyor orange exists in two values and they are not interchangeable. The bright flag measures 3.51:1 on the sheet — legal for large figures and for white-on-orange fills, and used for nothing else. Any orange text below large size uses the darkened ink (5.66:1). Do not simplify these back into one token; the split is what keeps the flag bright and the caveats readable.

rules.name: The Hi-Vis Is State Rule
rules.body: Yellow is never applied for emphasis, mood or branding inside the sheet. If a surface is hi-vis, something is logged, active, selected or tallied. If nothing is true of it, it is sheet or shade.

rules.name: The Cool Stock Rule
rules.body: The page ground is cool grey-green. Warming it toward cream breaks the waterproof-stock premise and is not a fix.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Measurement Rule
rules.body: Azeret Mono is reserved for things that were measured or recorded: record codes, figures, tallies, dates, units, and the small-caps labels that name them. Never a sentence of running prose, never atmosphere.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change while the user watches is set with tabular figures, so a tally never reflows its own digits.

rules.name: The 22px Pitch Rule
rules.body: The grid pitch is the rhythm. Vertical spacing should land near multiples of it rather than on an invented 4/8 scale, and nothing should tile over the ground so completely that the ruling disappears.

rules.name: The No-Lift Rule
rules.body: Nothing in this system lifts. If a surface needs to read as nearer, change its ground (shade → sheet), change its border weight, or invert it. Never add a shadow, and never a hard offset shadow, which belongs to a neobrutalist world this one is not.

rules.name: The Photograph Rule
rules.body: Species photographs are bundled in `assets/`, never hotlinked. The build shipped once with 17 dead Wikimedia URLs — files renamed upstream, every one 400ing — and hotlinking would re-earn that failure. Images are fetched from the Wikimedia API, licence-checked before download, cropped to 560×373 and re-encoded at q0.72 (4.68 MB of originals became 860 KB). Every photograph carries its author and licence on the plant sheet, and `CREDITS.md` lists all 17; a photo whose licence cannot be verified is not shipped at all. A photograph earns its place **at size** — it appears on the plant sheet and nowhere else, because at 58×44 in a list row a photo is mud while a drawn plate reads instantly. Plates and photographs are different jobs, not alternatives.

rules.name: The Taped-In Photograph Rule
rules.body: Photographs the user takes are stored as resized data URIs in `localStorage` and never leave the browser: no upload, no licence, nothing to rot. They are capped hard — 640px longest edge, JPEG q0.7, and a 3.2 MB total budget — because a phone photo is several megabytes and `localStorage` is a few. When the budget is spent the app says so in plain words rather than letting the write fail silently, and a removed sighting takes its photograph with it. This is the field notebook's own device: a photo taped to the page beside the entry.

rules.name: The Drawn Plate Rule
rules.body: Species imagery is authored SVG, not photography. Four line plates — Grass, Forb/herb, Shrub, Cactus — are drawn by growth form at 58×44 in `currentColor` on the shade ground, keyed off the record's category with Forb/herb as fallback. This is not a placeholder: a field guide draws its plates. It became the answer after all 17 inherited image URLs were found dead (every one 400s at Wikimedia), and it is the world's own solution, so future imagery extends the plate set rather than reverting to photos.

rules.name: The Icon Rule
rules.body: Icons are the Tabler webfont at its single outline weight, loaded from CDN and used across tick boxes, option toggles, buttons, the locality stamp, the plant sheet, the camera control, empty states and the wildlife log. Some are written into markup and the rest arrive from data records for wildlife groups, goals, sun options and marketplace entries. The exact count is deliberately not written here: it has gone stale three times in this file, once per feature that added a glyph. `.impeccable/design.json` carries the measured figure, and `grep -o 'ti-[a-z0-9-]*' index.html | sort -u | wc -l` is the authority. They are permitted because Tabler is a real drawn library at one consistent stroke, which is what the craft floor asks for — the refusal is Unicode glyphs and emoji standing in for an icon system, not a drawn icon set. Two constraints bind them here: icons take world ink only (`--graphite`, `--hivis`, `--survey`, `--stamp`) and never a per-item colour, which is the rule that removed ~15 inherited Material-palette hexes; and the CDN URL needs its `/dist/` path segment, without which the stylesheet 404s and every icon silently vanishes — the exact bug the superseded build shipped with. Icons label controls; species imagery is the plate set above, never an icon.

rules.name: The One Moment Rule
rules.body: This build spends its entire motion budget on the list re-rank: a FLIP over the plant list when a goal changes, so rows visibly travel to their new rank instead of silently re-rendering (420ms on `cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)`, transform only). It is guarded twice — a CSS `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` wrapper on the moving class, and a `matchMedia` early return in JS that skips the measurement entirely. Everything else in the system is 110–140ms colour and scale micro-state. A second authored moment is not free: adding one means removing this one.

rules.name: The Tally Rule
rules.body: Counts that accumulate render as real tally strokes, not as bars or dots: four uprights and a diagonal through each group of five, drawn as SVG at the graphite stroke. The THESIS promises a *tallied* list, and a generic chart would be the world breaking its own word. The wildlife run uses them for twelve months of sightings; any future count of observations uses them too.

rules.name: The Paperwork Is Generic Rule
rules.body: The before-you-dig checklist states requirements common across lawn-replacement programs and says so on the sheet. Writing a specific program's rules would be exactly the fabrication PRODUCT.md forbids, since none of them have been verified.

dos: Do keep the printed 22px grid on the page ground — two crossed linear-gradients in the rule colour at the grid pitch. It is the signature of the whole world.
Do split orange by size: the bright flag for fills and large figures, the darkened ink for any small text.
Do reserve hi-vis yellow for logged / active / tallied state.
Do set every code, figure, tally, date and label in Azeret Mono with tabular figures, and everything else in Archivo.
Do build depth from the three grounds and border weight (1px / 2px / 2.5px).
Do draw new species imagery as SVG plates by growth form, extending the existing plate set.

Do print truth as content, not as decoration: every rebate figure carries its own unverified line as body copy under a dashed surveyor-ink rule, a species outside the yard's climate band is flagged on its own row with a warn chip, and the marketplace states in its lede that it takes no commission. These are visual rules here, not copy to tidy away.
Do guard any motion twice — CSS prefers-reduced-motion and a JS matchMedia return.
donts: Don't add a box-shadow. There are none in this system, and a hard offset shadow in particular belongs to a neobrutalist world this one is not.
Don't add a corner radius. Zero, everywhere.
Don't warm the ground toward cream. The stock is cool by design.
Don't flatten the two oranges into one token, and don't set small text in the bright flag (3.51:1 — it fails AA below large sizes).
Don't replace the printed grid with a flat fill or tile a full-bleed surface over it.
Don't introduce a kicker or eyebrow line above a heading. The mono sub-label exists once, inside the brand lockup, and is not a pattern to repeat.
Don't use Azeret Mono for running prose or for atmosphere.
Don't add a second authored motion moment while the list re-rank stands.
Don't animate the tick box beyond its existing 110–120ms press; it is hit constantly.
Don't substitute photography for the drawn plates.
